entries.own_grammar_blurb: English does not assign ordinary nouns to grammatical masculine, feminine, or neuter classes. The article “the” stays the same. Gender can still appear in pronouns and vocabulary, but that is different from a noun-gender agreement system.
entries.comparison_blurb: English does not assign ordinary nouns to grammatical masculine, feminine, or neuter classes. The article “the” stays the same.

entries.own_grammar_blurb: En español, los sustantivos comunes pertenecen a dos géneros gramaticales: masculino y femenino. Los artículos y muchos adjetivos concuerdan con el sustantivo. También existen formas neutras como «lo», «esto», «eso» y «aquello», pero los sustantivos comunes no forman una tercera clase neutra.
entries.comparison_blurb: Spanish ordinary nouns belong to two grammatical genders: masculine and feminine. Articles and many adjectives agree with that gender. Spanish also has limited neuter forms, but ordinary nouns are not sorted into a third neuter class.
French has masculine and feminine grammatical noun gender. The contracted form l’ can hide the contrast before a vowel sound, so article spelling alone is not a perfect gender detector.
German has masculine, feminine, and neuter grammatical noun genders. Der, die, and das show the contrast in the nominative singular, while article forms also change with case and number.

Modern Greek has masculine, feminine, and neuter grammatical noun genders. The nominative singular definite articles ο, η, and το show the three-way contrast clearly; case and number create additional forms.

Russian has masculine, feminine, and neuter grammatical noun genders but no articles. Gender is visible through noun forms and agreement, so grammatical gender cannot be reduced to counting words meaning “the.”
Turkish does not assign ordinary nouns to masculine, feminine, or neuter grammatical gender classes.
Swahili uses a larger noun-class system with agreement across the phrase and sentence. It should not be flattened into a masculine/feminine/neuter count.
